aiSummary: The manuscript's epistemological argument centers on a *vertical* distinction from uncovering to knowledge, defending magic against naive idealism and realism through the distinction between *ordo essendi* and *ordo manifestationis*. It addresses the *horizontal* problem of epistemic diversity—how multiple minds with partial, deformed disclosures of the same world relate—particularly through ambiguity across alethic, doctrinal, and social/institutional registers. Alethic ambiguity involves ontological dislocation between actuality and intelligibility, doctrinal ambiguity stems from structural indeterminacy in phenomena, and social ambiguity arises from institutions with partial, conflicting disclosures. The framework defines epistemic diversity not as varied beliefs but as distinct modes of disclosure, where genuine diversity—seen in medical witnesses, priests, architects, and others—functions as a resource, not an obstacle. Agreement among witnesses may stem from shared failure, not independent insight, making institutional hegemony—the privileging of one description or credential—an epistemic failure.
title: Epistemic Diversity Analysis
